13:- Snow/winter services (round 123, 2026-09-23): independent pool nearly exhausted in corridor; 1 fresh qualifier (Grand Junction Landscaping, form-route WATCH). CMP Solutions LLC (Montrose, pipeline round 87, route UNKNOWN) is running a live limited-spots 2026-2027 winter campaign on Instagram (2026-09-04), the strongest current seasonal signal in the segment, but still publishes no own-site contact. SEO farms (thesnowremovalcompany.com, snowremoval-colorado.com, kandmlandscapes.com) and directory-only shops dominate the search surface; genuine independents are mostly landscape/property-service hybrids and phone-first.
22:- Insulation/pool/spa (batch 3, 17 candidates: 8 insulation, 9 pool/spa). Denver insulation is a crowded, rebate-driven market where nearly every small shop competes on free estimates and Xcel rebate paperwork, creating high inbound quote volume while owners and crews are on ladders or in attics; several reviews literally mention competitors never calling back. Pool/spa is thinner and more fragmented, a mix of franchise systems and true owner-operators, with year-round hot tub culture (weekly water care, Airbnb rentals, winter freeze repairs), so recurring-route operators miss urgent repair calls while driving routes. Both trades lean heavily on phone-first contact pages with few published emails.
32:- Appliance/handyman (batch 3, 21 candidates: 11 appliance, 10 handyman). Appliance repair is urgency-driven: same-day or next-day service, one to three hour arrival windows, phone-first booking; inbound calls arrive hot and a missed ring sends the customer to a competitor. Handyman businesses run on variety: project photos, estimates, and multi-trade job types require qualification and scheduling before dispatch, so their pain is sorting and follow-up rather than pure speed. Both trades are owner-led small teams with little or no office staff; only a handful publish a general email, and owner names are rarely stated, so outreach should lean on personalized angles tied to their posted promises rather than naming decision-makers.
40:- Foundation/masonry/drywall (batch 7, 25 candidates, 2026-09-09): new segments. Foundation repair & basement/crawlspace waterproofing (6 candidates): Mid-September 2026 is prime inspection season in Denver metro: monsoon rains and summer watering have swollen the area's expansive clay soils, so homeowners are discovering seepage, wall cracks, bowing basement walls, and drainage failures right as the pre-freeze window opens. Foundation and waterproofing jobs are high-ticket and almost always won or lost at first contact, and the owner-led shops here are typically in the field on jobs all day. Segment is clean of national brands in the small-shop tier (Groundworks, Thrasher, Ram Jack dealers all skipped as corporate/franchise). Watch for lead-broker style sites ("our network's experts" copy) that look like contractors but are not. Masonry & stucco (10 candidates): Mid-September 2026 is the last good stretch of Denver's exterior work window, and freeze-thaw season is approaching fast, exactly when homeowners discover cracked stucco, failing tuckpointing, and leaky chimney crowns, driving a rush of repair inquiries. Most shops are family-run crews of one to five people with the owner on the scaffold or at the job site, so incoming calls routinely go to voicemail or get answered after hours. Core pitch fit: AI call capture answers every ring, qualifies the repair, and books the free estimate, while automated follow-up keeps quotes from going cold. Skip pattern: multi-state branded stucco sites and larger remodelers that bundle stucco as one of many trades. Drywall & texture (9 candidates): September is the pivot point in Colorado as exterior work winds down and homeowners turn to basements, texture re-dos, popcorn ceiling removal, and water-damage repairs, so these shops want to keep crews busy with interior projects. The market is fragmented: dozens of owner-led shops of one to twenty people, most taking intake by phone or a basic contact form, many owners doubling as estimator and scheduler. Strongest fits are owner-operators (Benjamin at B&D Drywall, owner-run Flow Drywall) where every missed call is missed revenue; already-staffed firms are lower priority. Stay excluded: franchise systems (PatchMaster, Hole in the Wall, All Four Walls) whose local operators have less buying authority, plus thin AI-template sites and no-own-site directory-only operations.
42:- Handyman (Western CO, 4 candidates, 2026-09-09): fall is the busiest booking window: honey-do lists, deck/fence repairs, gutter cleaning, swamp-cooler winterization before the first hard freeze, heat-cable and pipe protection, holiday-guest prep punch lists. Second-home owners in Aspen/Snowmass/Steamboat send photo-based requests from out of town. Core pain: missed calls and slow estimates while the owner is on a ladder, plus estimate follow-up that dies when the day runs long; photo intake and estimate-chasing are the fit. Market is heavy with phone-only operators, directory-only listings, and dead sites; only own sites with a real email or form qualified.
47:- HVAC (Western Colorado, batch 13, 2026-09-09): new segment, 10 verified candidates. Independent, family-run, and employee-owned shops rather than national chains, anchored in Grand Junction, Montrose, Glenwood Springs with spokes into Aspen, Basalt, Durango, Hotchkiss, Cortez. September is the hinge month: furnace tune-ups, install-quote follow-up, first-cold-snap breakdowns, plus ski-town second homes needing reliable service from absentee owners. Nearly every shop runs its own site with a working contact form or published email, so direct outreach is practical. Skip patterns: phone-only own sites, parked/dead/hijacked domains, directory-only listings, and a Wheat Ridge-headquartered branch (Major Heating) deprioritized as not clearly local.
55:- Roofing (Western Colorado, batch 15, 2026-09-10): new segment, 11 verified candidates. Late-summer hail season winding down but roofers are in their busiest insurance-claim and free-inspection quarter; crews on roofs all day while phones go unanswered, so first-to-answer wins the claim. Coverage concentrated in Montrose (6), Grand Junction (2), Glenwood Springs (2), Durango (1), Gunnison (1); smaller markets yielded only directory/phone-only listings. Pattern: thin WordPress/Squarespace sites where the contact form is the only digital front door; several openly post Gmail/Yahoo addresses, signaling they live in their inboxes. Watch for lookalike regional chains and templated city pages.
60:- Septic / well / pump (Western Colorado, research batch round 23, 2026-09-11): new segment, 9 qualified. Septic pumping runs on 2 to 5 year recall cycles plus emergency demand; several shops promise free estimates and same-day/emergency service, creating the missed-call pain. 24/7 emergency positioning is everywhere but several shops run office-only hours; after-hours calls are the clearest AI receptionist angle. Durango is a septic hot spot (Durango Septic, Mountain Septic, LePew Four Corners, Alpenglow Gunnison). Well and pump shops (San Juan Pump, Valley Pump) have water-outage urgency: a homeowner with no water calls the next shop if the first rings out. Durango Septic literally brands on answering the phone ("the last thing you want is a voicemail") with a small crew in the field. No scheduling software observed anywhere in the segment; software grades UNKNOWN across the board. Segment is nearly all phone-only (8 of 9); only San Juan Pump (Montrose) has an unblocked contact form, though it is a customer form with no B2B invitation.
65:- Garage doors (Denver metro, research batch round 24, 2026-09-11): new segment (outward expansion), 9 qualified. Broken torsion springs are the single most urgent trigger; a door stuck open is a security emergency. Several shops advertise 24/7 but run daytime-only offices, so after-hours missed-call capture is the clean pitch. Segment is saturated with templated city-page SEO farms and a national franchise layer (A1, Precision, Dave's); Colorado-ownership verification stays mandatory. Watch address-sharing brands (A1 Garage Door Service shares 5081 Kingston St with Don's Garage Door Repair). Shops show little evidence of Housecall Pro style booking wizards; most routes are plain phone numbers or simple WordPress forms, so lead with missed-call capture rather than booking-friction relief. 7 Denver-area near-misses (Arvada Garage Door, AVI, Incredible, Mile High Sales & Repair, Garage Door Knights, DMAC, Gold Label Door) are BBB-listed with no own website; qualify on own-site discovery.
70:- House cleaning / maid services (Western Colorado, round 42, 2026-09-13): brand-new WCO segment; prior house-cleaning work was Denver-metro only, and WCO cleaning coverage stopped at carpet, duct, and commercial janitorial. The segment is rich in small owner-led shops with phone-only listings, which matches the missed-call angle precisely. Elite Cleaning Service (70+ employees, weekly recurring base) is the highest-value target; La Plata Cleaning carries a live missed-inquiry review signal. Franchises (Merry Maids GJ) and broker platforms (Walmart house cleaning, Care.com, Thumbtack, Turno, Homeaglow) were excluded. Sparkling and Beyond RE-VERIFIED from the 2026-09-13 archive (own-site email + phone now confirmed on its FAQ page) but held on WATCH: its site shows TN and IA city pages, so local ownership must be verified before any outreach.
71:- Epoxy / concrete coatings (Western Colorado, round 55, 2026-09-14): brand-new WCO segment. Independent pool is genuinely thin once chains are removed: national/regional systems (Garage Kings, GarageFloorCoating.com dealer network with pages for nearly every Western Slope town, Spartan Floor Coatings) dominate search visibility. Remaining independents are small owner-operated shops in the northwest and mountain corridors (Craig, Steamboat, Roaring Fork, Pagosa), plus painters for whom epoxy floor coatings are a secondary line (Mountain Sky Closets and Garages, Todd Hill Painting, Sloop Painting). Recurring pattern: phone-only intake, no email/form/follow-up machinery, which is exactly the missed-call opening but only WATCH-grade until verified per business. Pre-winter pitch angle supported by multiple coating sites (garage floor protection against snowmelt, road salts, freeze-thaw), but keep it generic, not personalized, until a business-specific problem is verified. Skip patterns: chain/dealer systems (Garage Kings, GarageFloorCoating.com pages, Spartan), out-of-state SEO location pages (Florida company running a Cortez page), generic lead-gen toll-free pages, athletic-court-only resurfacing, Front Range companies.
72:- Awning / shade / patio covers (Western Colorado, round 55, 2026-09-14): brand-new WCO segment. Specialist pool is genuinely sparse as of September 2026: two deep specialists verified (Canvas Shade in GJ, third-generation since 1949, structured multi-step intake form, owner named on site, the clearest WARM in the pool; Durango Shade Company, Wix site, motorized shade systems by phone), two Montrose-area owner-operators (Alpine Shades, motorized/smart-home products, phone-only; Colorado Awning and Screen, Eclipse retractable specialist, own site failed to render this round), one GJ retractable-awning specialist (Western Slope Shading Solutions, WordPress, no own-site contact found), one Glenwood contractor (Daybreak, aging site, awning is one service line, revamp candidate). Mid-September timing is tail-end for shade sales season (commercial restaurant patio enclosures and residential shade sails sell hardest in spring/early summer); fall angle is commercial patio enclosure and off-season planning. Skip patterns: interior window-treatment showrooms (Ambassador Blind, Shades Done Right, Budget Blinds, Gotcha Covered = franchises), general deck/fence builders, Front Range companies, national manufacturers, directory/lead-broker pages, tent manufacturers.
73:- Pest control (Western Colorado, research batch round 68, 2026-09-16): new geography for an old segment. Vertebrate specialists (prairie-dog crews) and one family pest shop in GJ; most are directory-only or phone-only, so the strict own-site rule kept the pest batch small (4). Pool/spa/hot tub (Western Colorado, research batch round 68, 2026-09-16): 11 qualified, the richest WCO batch in several rounds. Three CONFIRMED stack finds: HubSpot forms on Colorado Pool + Spa Scapes (response-speed gap, not lead-volume), Wix on Four Corners Stoves and Spa, MyPoolPortal customer portal on Telluride Spa Care (portal angle dead, AI answering and route scheduling open). Route-based trades with strong missed-call angles; several owner-led shops with no websites at all (Tub Tech Spas, operating since 1987). Eight directory-only records have blank contact fields per the no-guessing rule.
76:- Smart-home / security-system installers (Western Colorado, round 74, 2026-09-17): brand-new WCO segment. Independent pool is thin and fragmented: GJ has Superior Alarm Inc, Fire Team Security, EyeCamTech and a handful of small AV/surveillance shops; Durango shows directory-thin AV/security names; Montrose/Telluride show Superior Alarm & Fire Protection, a distinct entity from GJ's Superior Alarm Inc. Segment heat: moderate; alarm shops run phone-only intake competing against Vivint and ADT on local trust, and a 3-star or lower review mentioning phone or response issues is a strong trigger for this trade. Pitch angle: after-hours alarm and camera calls go to voicemail while techs are on installs, so missed-call capture plus fast callback is the core ROI story; website revamp is secondary (several sites are thin or template-built). Skip pattern: multi-state ADT dealer models with local offices stay WATCH only; MSPs masquerading as security shops (CommWest) and directory-only listings with no own site stay at WATCH. Note: Superior Alarm Inc and Commwest were already pipeline NEW from round 52; this round re-verified own-site phone (970-245-0962) and own-site email/phone (concierge@commwestcorp.com, 970-242-8124) instead of creating duplicate rows.
78:- Tree care / arborists (Mesa County corridor re-run, round 100, 2026-09-20): 7 qualified, corridor towns only. Segment heat is high: EAB confirmed on the Western Slope (Carbondale, Sept 2026) is a live market-level demand driver, and the fall pre-winter hazard-tree window is open; September-April is the dormant period for ash pruning/removal per town guidance. Missed-call economics dominate: crews are on ropes or storm work while emergency and tree-health calls land on a single phone line, often outside 7:30-17:00 business hours. ISA certification is the published trust differentiator (GJ and Carbondale government lists). Dead/thin web presence is the norm for independents (one candidate's domain is suspended and for sale while the business still operates). Chain watch: SavATree has absorbed T4, Peak Tree Works, Alpine, and Aspen Tree Service between earlier research and send day; re-verify independence at outreach time, never just at discovery. Email-route yield was 1 of 7 (own-site rule held); the rest are phone-route NEWs or form-only. Note: Highlands Tree Co (Carbondale, HOT, phone-only) is the top phone-route tree candidate; it modernizes its own site (Vercel), so the angle there is intake automation, not revamp.
82:- Handyman (Mesa County corridor re-run, round 106, 2026-09-21): 3 found, 1 dropped on audit, 2 added (Kokopelli Home Services GJ form-route HOT, owners Dana & Ben Russell named; Four Seasons Maintenance Montrose form-route WARM, Wix CONFIRMED, handyman scope is secondary-category evidence so confirm a services page before a strong pitch). 34 names researched, 31 excluded. Dominant exclusion pattern: phone-only own sites among one-operator shops with real local reputations (Little Lions, Roberts Maintenance/GJ Handyman since 1992, Redtail Home Solutions, Ward's) but no compliant route; re-check later. Lead-broker noise is heavy (Handy Does It, Bro's Handyman with 855 routing). Season: late September is the last warm-weather window for exterior handyman work (decks, fences, swamp-cooler shutdowns); shops are stacked and estimate follow-up is where leads die, so speed-to-lead and missed-call follow-up while the owner is on a job is the honest angle.
83:- Fence-staining restoration + log-home restoration (round 127, 2026-09-23): two new segments, honest yield 2 of 15-25 target. Pencil Log Pros (GJ, office@pencillogpros.com own-site email, owner Brad Siler, 16+ employees, CONFIRMED confidence) is the log-home specialist anchor; Every Fence GJ (fencerepairgj.com own-site form, Weebly STRONG INDICATION, WATCH) is the fence-staining fit. Late September is the final reliable exterior staining window before cold/wet weather; log-home work is in the fall pre-winter inspection/sealing window. Surfaces are thin: fence-staining dominated by broad painters, lead-broker directories (OutdoorNearMe, Porch), out-of-area firms (R&J Painting = Illinois; FenceMakeover = Front Range; Pure Pressure = Northern CO round-89 exclusion), already-tracked names (RJ's Painting, Valleywide, Just Fencing, Taylor Fence, Top Choice), no-own-site specialists (StainMisters GJ, Mountain Life Custom Staining Montrose), one hijacked-content site (Final Touch Painting renders VA roofing copy). Log-home near-misses: kit manufacturer/builder Frontier Log Homes (Montrose, off-segment), identity-conflicted Mountain State Log Homes, out-of-geography specialists (Jorgensen SD, Tuks Steamboat). New-business radar: The Screen Medic (screen repair/install) opened a new GJ location (1700 I-70BL #2), ribbon-cut by GJ Area Chamber 2026-09-23, expansion of existing Montrose shop (NOT a new filing); MN name-twin unresolved, recheck chain at outreach time. GJ Chamber ribbon-cutting pipeline is the highest-signal radar channel right now (2 cuttings in 12 days); SOS still JS-only; chamber new-member lists still not surfaced. FB scan #126 (52 in-window): 1 new prospect (The Yellow handyman services, Delta-area, FB Page route only, message-button check pending); corridor FB trade-promo volume near zero seven windows running. Review intel: 0 triggers across 10-prospect HOT/WARM sample (RAM price-transparency complaint undated = angle material only). AEO: Alpine Pressure STRONG (already AEO-literate, not an opportunity); RAM MODERATE (review-volume + town/service FAQ gap); Grime Fighters MODERATE (severe AEO namesake crowding: PA/TN/NC/GA firms dilute identity); Mr Patch MODERATE (strong content trapped on Google Sites/Wix subdomains, own-domain migration opportunity).
85:- Foundation repair / waterproofing (round 135, 2026-09-24, WCO geography pass): 16 researched, 0 staged. Chain/dealer captured: Groundworks (acquired Foundation Repair of Western Colorado), Supportworks dealer (Aspen Foundation Repairs, already WATCH), Basement Systems dealers (Silver River, Colorado Crawl Space), Pueblo-regional (Colorado Structural Repair). One independent WATCH: Tom Peters / "Colorado Foundation Repair" (Fruita, phone-only, no genuine own site; coloradofoundationrepair.com is a Front Range SEO lead-farm). Segment is project/estimate-driven, so missed-call fit is WEAKER than emergency trades; angle is free-estimate lead capture while crews are on job sites. Seasonal why-now: monsoon + summer irrigation swelling expansive soils, pre-freeze inspection season.
